How Do I Know If I Have a Personal Injury Case? Generally speaking, a personal injury case allows the victim of an avoidable accident to seek compensation from a negligent or otherwise liable party. You may have the ability to bring a personal injury claim if you got hurt: In a San Diego traffic accident because another driver was careless On the job in San Diego Due to a dangerous condition on someone else’s property While using a defective product As a result of a medical professional’s negligence When you were attacked by an animal You may also have the right to bring a personal injury lawsuit if you’ve experienced the wrongful death of a family member in a San Diego accident. Explore your legal options and understand your rights by speaking with our trusted California personal injury attorneys in San Diego today. We can evaluate your situation, explain your options, and help you fight for the accountability you deserve. How Much is My San Diego Personal Injury Case Worth? Your story is one of a kind. The experience you’ve had is like no other. So, it makes sense that the value of your personal injury claim will be unique, too. Several factors will potentially impact how much money you may be able to recover through a personal injury claim: How were you injured? What physical injuries have you suffered? Are your injuries severe? Are you temporarily or permanently disabled? Can you continue to work? Have you experienced a change in your earning capacity, income, or benefits? Do you share responsibility for the accident? Did the accident aggravate a pre-existing condition? Is the defense blaming you for your injuries? What insurance benefits are available to you? How old are you? What’s your life expectancy? How have the accident and resulting trauma affected your quality of life? When it comes to valuation, the severity of your injuries will tend to be the most influential factor. Catastrophic injuries can cost victims tens of thousands, hundreds of thousands, or millions of dollars over the course of a lifetime. As a result, more severe injuries tend to result in higher financial recoveries. However, shared fault, a failure to mitigate damages, and other factors can drive down the value of a claim. Learn more about the potential value of your personal injury case and increase the odds of a maximum recovery by turning to Singleton Schreiber after your San Diego accident. We’ve helped our clients win million-dollar and multi-million dollar recoveries. We’ll fight to get you top results, too. What Compensation is Available to Accident Victims in San Diego? While there are some exceptions, most personal injury plaintiffs are able to seek compensatory damages through an insurance claim or lawsuit. Compensatory damages are further divided into two categories, economic awards and non-economic awards. Each aims to compensate victims for different types of losses. Economic Damages Economic damages are intended to offset the financial losses and costs associated with an accident and resulting trauma, such as: Current and future medical bills Disability Reduced earning capacity Lost income and wages Rehabilitation and therapy Out-of-pocket expenses Nursing assistance Funeral costs Economic damages are limited to your verified and reasonably projected financial losses. You’ll need to support your claim with proof in the form of receipts, invoices, wage statements, and other documentation. Non-Economic Damages Non-economic damages are intended to help you, as a victim, cope with trauma and life experiences that are more difficult to value, such as: Chronic physical pain Physical disfigurement and scarring Loss of enjoyment of life Loss of consortium Pain and suffering Post-traumatic stress disorder Inconvenience Emotional distress Since these damages are so personal and intimate, they’re often hotly contested during negotiations. Our personal injury attorneys in San Diego will enlist highly respected experts to help us fully understand how your injuries have affected your life - both financially and personally. When it’s time to negotiate, we’ll have compelling evidence to prove just how devastating your accident and injuries have been. Can Contributory Negligence Impact My California Personal Injury Settlement? Yes, sharing responsibility for an accident will have an unwanted impact on your ability to recover compensation. Under California’s pure comparative negligence system, any settlements or jury awards will be reduced proportionately to fault. Let’s say you’re severely injured in a San Diego car accident. Your case is valued to be worth one million dollars. However, since you were speeding at the time of the wreck, you’re assigned 50 percent of the blame. As a result, your maximum financial recovery will be cut in half, leaving you with $500,000 in damages. You’ll need to be ready to challenge any claims of shared responsibility. The more fault you’re assigned, the smaller your take-home financial award will be. Our San Diego personal injury attorneys will anticipate victim-blaming tactics and be prepared to fight them with the full force of our law firm’s resources and experience. What Will I Need to Prove to Win My San Diego Personal Injury Case? Negligence is the primary cause of action for personal injury lawsuits in the state of California. You’ll have a negligence action if you’ve suffered injuries because of another party’s careless or reckless conduct. When your personal injury lawsuit is based on negligence, you will have the burden of proving four distinct elements: Duty of Care: A defendant will only be liable if it can be demonstrated that they owed you a duty of care. This generally involves a responsibility to use caution and comply with local, state, and federal law. Breach of Duty: The defendant must breach the duty of care to you in some way. You must prove that their actions or failure to act deviated from expected conduct and were unreasonable under the circumstances. Causation: It’s not enough for the defendant to breach of duty of care to you. Their conduct must have also been the direct and proximate cause of your injury. You have to show that you would likely not have been injured if it hadn’t been for the defendant’s actions. Damages. You must be able to identify specific damages, such as medical expenses, a loss of income, or emotional distress. The specific standards of care can vary from one type of personal injury case to another. Don’t struggle to build a successful negligence action on your own. Trust our San Diego personal injury attorneys to invest their considerable experience and resources into building a winning case for you. What Are the Chances My Personal Injury Lawsuit Will Go to Trial? Slim. Roughly 4 to 5 percent of personal injury cases to get the trial stage. The majority are settled privately between parties. Ultimately, several things can influence whether your case settles or moves forward to a jury: What does the insurance company/defense believe the personal injury case is worth? What do you believe your personal injury case is worth? How strong is the evidence you have proving liability and establishing your damages? Has the insurance company offered you a fair settlement offer? Has the insurance company handled your claim in bad faith? Keep in mind that the decision to accept a settlement or go to trial is yours. When you receive a settlement offer, you have the power to accept it, extend a counter, or reject it altogether. One way to increase the odds of pressing the insurance company into offering a substantial settlement is by hiring a respected California trial attorney to represent you. When you make it clear that you’re ready to go to court, the insurance company might be more inclined to offer a higher settlement out of the gate. Learn more about our fee structure and why you will definitely want to have our top-rated legal team fight for you. What is California’s Statute of Limitations for Personal Injury Cases? You will have a limited amount of time to pursue compensation after an accident in San Diego, California. Typically, a two-year statute of limitations applies to personal injury and wrongful death cases. There are some exceptions, including: Child Injury: The two-year statute of limitations is tolled until the child’s 20th birthday Government Tort Claim: You must file an administrative claim with the government within 6 months of your accident. Property Damage: Claims for property damages are subject to a three-year statute of limitations. Workers’ Compensation: You have one year from the date of your on-the-job injury or diagnosis of a work-related illness to file a claim for workers’ compensation benefits. You have to file your personal injury claim before the applicable deadline passes. When time expires, you will lose the ability to seek damages from an insurance company or at-fault party.
